# cp

Copy files and directory trees to new destinations through MoonX.

## Usage

```sh
moonx cli/cp --no-preserve=mode source.txt new.txt

moonx cli/cp --no-preserve=mode -R source-dir new-dir
```

Copying requires --no-preserve=mode. Recursive copies check the source tree before creating destinations; explicit skip modes can succeed without copying.

## Common options

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OPTIONS -->
<!-- Generated by tools/metadata from options.json. -->

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-R`, `--recursive` | Copy directory trees. |
| `-n`, `--no-clobber` | Skip existing targets. |
| `--update=MODE` | Select the documented destination update policy. |
| `-L`, `--dereference` | Select source-link traversal. |
| `-T`, `--no-target-directory` | Treat destination as a complete path. |
| `--no-preserve VALUE` | Required for copying to a new destination. |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show copied paths. |
| `--help` | Show help. |
| `--version` | Show the version. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

Use `--help` for the complete option list.

## Notes

- Existing-file replacement, default mode preservation and archive copies are unsupported. Parsed -f, -i and backup options do not enable these operations.
- Source-link traversal must be selected explicitly where needed. Cycles and destinations inside the source are rejected.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md) for the supported profile.
